quietus.title: Matt Carmichael on New Album and EFG London Jazz Festival Appearance
quietus.description: Matt Carmichael speaks to Gail Tasker about his lush combination of jazz and folk, Held In The Dark, which will be performed with a full septet at three shows next month including a set for EFG London Jazz Festival Photo by Camille Lemoine Matt Carmichael is an artist whose deep and introspective relationship with music belies his years. Based in Glasgow, he forms part of a cohort of young music graduates who have steadily yet organically been pushing against the boundaries of learned traditions. Carmichael’s latest album, Held In The Dark, is his fourth, and a further iteration of the lush combination of folk and jazz which characterises his music. In some ways, Held In The Dark is…

quietus.title: Ye Gods – Los
quietus.description: Ye Gods Los Visited by the ghost of gothmas past, Antoni Maiovvi whips out his magic circle for a true grimoire of an album Los by Ye Gods When Killing Joke’s Jaz Coleman tells you to do something, you should probably do it. Even if it’s only in a dream. In the case of British composer Antoni Maiovvi (AKA AD Goodfellow), the post-punk vocalist’s mid-slumber visit guided him back to the ritual magick practice he had let slide. To further atone for this oversight, Coleman suggested the name Ye Gods. Seven years and 12 releases later (by my abacus twiddling) and this “occult devotional electronics project” arrives at the William Blake-referencing Los. Over the years, Maiovvi’s compositional…

quietus.title: The Electro Quartet – Nature’s World With Studio G
quietus.description: The Electro Quartet Nature’s World With Studio G An album of electronic library music from the early 80s breaths the air of sunnier climes Nature's World With Studio G by Various Artists 1982 was an odd year. Ozzy Osbourne was treated for rabies after biting the head of a bat in the middle of a gig. The first ever computer virus was created by a 15-year old kid in Pittsburgh. Mary Whitehouse sued the National Theatre for obscenity. The Falklands War kicked off in the South Atlantic. Israel invaded Lebanon in a military campaign called Operation Peace. Abba split up. The first compact discs were produced in Germany. The most popular albums in Britain that year included Barbra Streisand’s…

quietus.title: Beyond The Pleasuredome: Frankie Goes To Hollywood’s Liverpool 40 Years On
quietus.description: Wyndham Wallace looks at the oft-neglected follow-up to FGTH's debut, Liverpool which was released in 1986 Compare and contrast: "The world is my oyster," the opening words to Frankie Goes To Hollywood's debut album, 1984's Welcome To The Pleasuredome. Delivered by Holly Johnson in the flippant style of a cartoon villain, a cackling laugh in their wake. "I'm looking for something and I don't know what it is," the last words to Frankie Goes To Hollywood's second and final album, 1986's Liverpool. Delivered by Holly Johnson in the style of a man running on empty, almost bereft of hope. What a difference a couple of years can make. Frankie Goes To Hollywood first hit the top of the UK charts…

quietus.title: An Evergreen Lodestar of all that is Abominable: How Reign in Blood Changed Metal
quietus.description: Ian Winwood looks back 40 years to his first contact with an imperial and imperious Slayer and their third album's "frenzied scream of wall-eyed mayhem" On the weekend before Christmas, in 2020, I sent a friend a text message comprised of just three words. It read: Epidemic. Permanent disease. I had no doubt that my old familiar would recognise the bulletin as being a snippet of a lyric from Reign In Blood, by Slayer. Thirty-four years earlier, while listening for the first time to an import edition of the album dispatched by post from Shades Records, in Soho, the two of us had been forever conjoined by the fiercest musical experience of our teenage lives. We’d stood transfixed in the…

quietus.title: Fisherman’s Blues: the Damning Indictment cast by All Rivers Spill Their Stories To The Sea
quietus.description: Claire Sawers talks to director Jeanie Finlay about her hard-hitting, emotionally resonant documentary about toxic pollution of UK waters, which doubles as love letter to the north east Stan Rennie takes a tea break, by Jeanie Finlay “I’m sick as a chip”, says Stan Rennie. He’s dressed in shiny orange fisherman’s bibs and lifejacket, sat aboard his blue and white boat, the Sarah Lynn, on the waters around Hartlepool. That particular Northernism nails his beyond fed up feeling. We’d say ‘seek’ in Scots. Flattened by the injustice of his situation and we’re right there with him. It’s at the end of the documentary All Rivers Spill Their Stories To The Sea and we’re glimpsing a rare moment of…

quietus.title: New Weird Britain in Review for October, by Noel Gardner
quietus.description: Your latest guide to the British underground comes with bananas mashcore from a huge crew of Rotherham children, a demonstration of the discombobulatory potential of the human voice, and much more V.I.V.E.K Unfathomable amounts of music are being recorded around the world daily, more than you could hear in a thousand lifetimes with access to a server bigger than the Ritz. And even then, not everything is getting captured. Think how many formalised music-making sessions are happening somewhere, as I write and you read. The participants are likely finding their feet and letting off steam, not attempting to create something for public consumption. But what if someone involved realises the…

Frontman Lukas Frank has dabbled in soundtracks as well as having a few bits of acting on his CV, so if anyone knows what he’s doing, he does. Having stepped out from...

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ghost Dubs :: Oblique
aquariumdrunkard.description: On his second album as Ghost Dubs , German producer Michae Fiedler pares his beats and grooves further back, reducing his already minimal palette to the stark rhythmic and textural fundamentals. But the tracks on Oblique resist the remoteness of some ambient dub — they might be skeletal, but they’re not bare-bones.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Joe Casey of Protomartyr (2026)
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on Transmissions, we're speaking with return guest Joe Casey of Protomartyr. The band's new album, Hotel Usona is a timely meditation on our empire in decline but also a document of defiance and even a kind of hope. Check in, tune out.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Fela Kuti & Africa ’70 :: Live in Berlin (Berliner Jazztage, 1978)
aquariumdrunkard.description: No retreat. No surrender. Filmed at the Berliner Jazztage on November 4, 1978, with Tony Allen still at the kit, this 87-minute document captures Fela Kuti and Africa ’70 at the end of their Herculean run. Unearthed decades later, the tapes capture the collective’s internal chemistry intact at the very moment its future was set to fracture.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Introducing Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard: Longform Listening. Worldwide. 24/7.
aquariumdrunkard.description: A Continuous Broadcast from Aquarium Drunkard. Hand-curated. No playlists. Nothing to scroll. Nothing random. Everything intentional. Transmitting from the hills of Northeast Los Angeles, Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard is a free, always-on radio station. Press play and you're tuned in to what's on the air right now, alongside everyone else. The broadcast continues and tracks advance whether or not you're listening. The app is free, but requires an active Apple Music subscription. James Barnes is the architect. Justin Gage is the selector.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me (Soundtrack, Angelo Badalamenti)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Mid-October approaches, and the owls are not what they seem. The best records belong to a particular hour, season, or state of mind. aquariumdrunkard.title: PAINT :: Whip of an Ear
aquariumdrunkard.description: No one is making music quite like PAINT, the project of musician and Allah-Las guitarist Pedrum Siadatian. If a song title can be prophetic, it's "Illusion of Voice" here, in which the vocals of real and hypothetical cast of ensemble characters and collaborators weave through a shadowy labyrinth full of twists of surrealistic transparency. From police blotter audio soundscapes to warbled poetry reads, fourth record Whip of an Ear is an obtusely captivating listen and one of the prolific musician's best offerings yet.

mubi.title: Masao Adachi: Demystifying a Legend

Born in 1939 in Kyushu, Japan, he moved to Tokyo to attend Nihon University, coming of age during the turbulent protests against the renewal of the mutual security treaty between Japan and the United States in 1959–60. He started making films with a student group and soon emerged as one of the leading figures in the burgeoning underground cinema scene. In the mid-1960s, Adachi became involved with the sexploitation industry, writing and directing several striking examples of the genre for Koji Wakamatsu’s production company. W. When Élisabeth was released to blanket disinterest, Scherer began to branch out from literature into film criticism, and, later, filmmaking. With each new endeavor, the pseudonyms piled up. This culture of ultravoyagers embarked on their own age of exploration while Europe was still mired in the Middle Ages, colonizing the tiny islands dotting the South Pacific without the benefit of metal tools, navigational equipment, or a written language.
